prompt: Design a REVIEW-ONLY visual concept for BENCHMATE, an iPhone companion guiding a novice to make a small cat figurine using a Bambu X1 Carbon. User rejected the previous app: too little contrast, weak hierarchy, too many buttons and decisions. User asks for a SIMPLE STEP-BY-STEP GAMIFIED experience inspired by Duolingo's focus and encouraging progression, while remaining aesthetic and creative. Do not copy Duolingo branding, owl, green palette, exact layouts or punitive mechanics. Keep a real 3D sculptural cat and distinctive matte/frosted glass. Show FOUR large legible phone screens in one clean 16:9 board, with only tiny external captions. Structure: 1 FOCUSED TASK 'Check your plate.' with gold textured plate model, concise readable line 'Clean, dry, and seated flat.' and ONE strong primary button 'Plate checked'; top context '02 / Ready the printer', a compact progress indicator, one quiet help '?' affordance and small back arrow. 2 EARNED CHECKPOINT 'One step closer.' with same cat and a single beautiful earned chapter check/faceted token, short 'Printer setup reviewed.' and ONE 'Next: the first layer' button. This celebrates a recorded user check, not automatic machine safety. 3 RECOVERY 'A fresh start.' with original 3D plate and detergent/sponge, 'End the failed job. Let the hardware cool before cleaning.' and ONE main 'Review the next step' action, quiet help; calm coral/amber issue cue, no penalty. 4 PERSONAL FINISH 'Meet Miso.' with same cat, short gift context, progress complete and ONE 'Keep my project' action. Treat this as a labeled guided demo; no claim a real print exists. Keep tiny persistent Demo text unobtrusive. Every screen has exactly ONE visually dominant primary action. No camera selector, rotate buttons, tab bar, equipment card, source link row, save button, standalone progress menu, wall of checks, permanent reward inventory, competing calls to action, XP score, streak, hearts, timer, notification badges or catalog. Secondary resources are reachable through the quiet help affordance, not displayed as choices. Product is the hero with ample calm space. Never reduce actual necessary physical checks to an unsafe shortcut; chapter labels group microsteps, do not promise completion in four taps. Text hierarchy must be unmistakable: large dark bold heading, medium near-black 16-17pt task copy, subdued but readable 12pt progress label. Use charcoal/navy #182733 text on warm mineral-white #F3F0EC with generous contrast. Strong action accent: deep saturated glacier teal #075C7D with white button label; use luminous orange/peach #F58C5A as a small energetic marker/reward accent. Glass is cloudy and almost opaque behind text, with selective frosted bevels and cyan/amber rim light. The reference palette must be visible, not a washed-out monochrome app. Cat material: satin opal frost with warm peach upper highlights, cool glacier-blue lower/side shading, creamy transition, fine additive-layer grain, rounded pear body, large rounded head, soft ears, tiny face, feet and curled tail; SAME cat across screens. Original geometry and studio lighting, not a flat illustration or transparent hologram. Its multicolor shading is visualization styling, not a physical PLA promise. STATIC concept only: no animation or camera motion. Generated text is illustrative; not equipment-procedure authority. No image uploads or external search. Synthesize ALL NINE user references into one original design, not a collage. 1 lavender 3D office: prominent spatial object, avoid dashboard/sidebar/room. 2 gray-yellow technical valve: precise geometry and selective accent, avoid telemetry. 3 two mobile valve screens: oversized central object and sparse lower task controls, primary mobile proportions. 4 exploded keyboard switch: studio lighting and physical material depth, avoid branding/exploded cat. 5 cobalt-orange fluted glass: narrow ribbed/faceted edges, avoid busy backdrop. 6 matte green tile study: cloudy diffusion, milky boundaries, fine grain, avoid tile grid and green-dominant palette. 7 peach-cyan/mint-coral frosted tiles: warm/cool diffusion and micrograin, avoid copying tile layout. 8 standing orange/cyan/navy glass slabs: material thickness and luminous edges, avoid dark UI and low contrast transparent text panels. 9 frosted wayfinding slabs: thick translucent bevels and cloudy warm/cool centers, avoid copied signage/text/icons. DIRECTION B — POCKET QUEST. More playful and habitually inviting without childish cartoon clutter. A strong small circular chapter marker with a five-part colored ring, bold friendly sans headlines, one hero object on a sculpted frosted plinth, a more tactile dimensional teal primary action, small apricot chapter/reward stamp. Stage completion is visually satisfying through a single 3D frosted gem/check token next to the familiar cat; no floating confetti or extra buttons. Introduce one deliberate warm-peach curved color field balancing ice-blue glass, while most screen stays pale and legible. Keep the layout concentrated into a short readable path, current action obvious. Fun comes from material, shape, color and visible accomplishment, not points or pressure. Board title 'B / Pocket quest'.
